isolation: separate process, environment without credentials, 120 s timeout, own temporary folder; macOS sandbox: no network, no .env reads, writes only inside that folder
explanation: The R script fits glm(target ~ <all train columns except row_id, target, SEX, AGE, ID>, family = binomial(logit)) with an intercept, predicts response-scale probabilities on test, and classifies with probability >= 0.35. The Python module selects the same features in the same column order, builds the design matrix directly (avoiding formula parsing problems with non-syntactic names, since read.csv used check.names = FALSE), adds an intercept, and fits sm.GLM with a Binomial family and logit link, which uses IRLS like R. Numeric columns enter linearly. Non-numeric columns get R-style treatment contrasts, with the first sorted level as the reference and unused levels dropped. Training rows with missing values are dropped, as R's na.omit does. predict_proba returns the inverse-logit of the linear predictor. classify applies the >= 0.35 threshold.
assumptions: target is coded numerically as 0/1 (or boolean); a factor/character target is not handled.
Numeric columns are used as-is with no transformation; there are no interactions or splines.

Character and boolean predictors are treated as R factors with treatment contrasts. The reference level is the first in sorted order. This may differ from R's locale-based sort for mixed-case strings.
Rows with any missing value in target or predictors are dropped before fitting (glm default na.action = na.omit). Unused factor levels are dropped (glm uses drop.unused.levels = TRUE).
If a test row has missing predictors, its probability is NaN. R would return NA. classify labels such rows 0, whereas R would give NA.
An unseen factor level in the test data raises an error, as R's predict does.
The design matrix is assumed to be full rank. R would set aliased coefficients to NA, which this port does not replicate.
No prior weights or offset are used, matching the R call.

term_mapping.note: Keeps the same columns in the same order.
Additive main effects plus an intercept.
